# End-to-end Python detection pipeline

Deliver a working, runnable near-duplicate detector for Python test files: AST extraction, normalisation, shingle/Jaccard similarity, inverted index, basic clustering, CLI, and JSON + Markdown output. This is the tracer-bullet slice — it goes from test-file collection through to written reports in one deliverable.

## Parent AC coverage

This task covers **AC1 (structural detection)** — Python test blocks detected via ast with docstrings stripped, identifiers replaced by positional placeholders, literals canonicalised to type placeholders so a renamed copy still matches; never raw text equality. Also covers **AC2 (clusters reported with location and score)** for the Python path — each cluster lists member file paths, start-end line ranges, block sizes, similarity scores and redundancy measure; JSON + Markdown written to --output-dir. Also covers **AC4 (performance bounds)** — inverted shingle index used instead of all-pairs; --min-lines, --threshold defaults.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 - Detection is structural, not textual. Near-duplicate test blocks are detected within and across files using normalised representation: Python test blocks via ast (docstrings stripped, identifiers replaced by positional placeholders, literals canonicalised to type placeholders so a renamed copy still matches), JavaScript/TypeScript/other test files via comment-stripped token normalisation with brace-matched block boundaries. Raw text equality is never the similarity measure. (This slice delivers the Python part; JS/TS follows in the next slice.)
- AC2 - Clusters are reported with location and score. Each cluster lists every member's file path, start-end line range, block size (lines and tokens), member-to-member and cluster similarity score, and a redundancy measure (member lines minus the largest member's lines) used to order the report. Both test_duplicates.json (versioned schema: thresholds, method, limitations, clusters) and test_duplicate_report.md (human, same content, ordered by redundancy) are written to --output-dir. (This slice delivers the Python path end-to-end.)
- AC3 - Python block extraction: top-level functions, classes, methods, and with-wrapped test bodies are extracted with file path and start-end line range.
- AC4 - Python normalisation: docstrings removed, identifiers replaced by positional placeholders per lexical scope, literals canonicalised to type placeholders (string to {str}, int to {int}, etc.), whitespace collapsed.
- AC5 - Token k-gram shingle generation (k default 5), Jaccard similarity, and inverted shingle index producing candidate pairs without all-pairs O(n^2) comparison.
- AC6 - Basic transitive clustering of blocks above threshold, redundancy measure (member lines minus largest member lines), clusters ordered by total redundant lines descending.
- AC7 - CLI accepts: --project-root, --output-dir, --min-lines N, --threshold, and --quiet. Shaped like the churn analyser CLI.
- AC8 - test_duplicate_report.md and test_duplicates.json written with method, thresholds, limitations and cluster data; one-line summary printed to stderr.
- AC9 - Output is deterministic: same tree and flags produce byte-identical JSON; non-deterministic sources (file system order) are sorted.
- AC10 - Unit tests cover: Python AST extraction of async tests, parametrised tests and nested classes; normalisation invariance (renamed copy scores >= threshold); distinct behaviour below band; shingle and Jaccard behaviour; inverted index correctness; basic clustering and redundant-line arithmetic; JSON and Markdown schema/content; deterministic output; empty/single-block suite.
- AC11 - skill/test-churn/SKILL.md gains a Near-duplicate detection section and docs/dev/test-churn-skill-reference.md gains a skeleton recording the method and thresholds; both updated in this slice, not deferred.

## Deliverables

- skill/test-churn/scripts/test_duplicate_detection.py - Python extraction, normalisation, shingling, Jaccard, inverted index, basic clustering, CLI, JSON/MD writers
- skill/test-churn/tests/test_test_duplicate_detection.py - unit + e2e tests for the Python pipeline
- skill/test-churn/tests/conftest.py - path-loaded fixture for test_duplicate_detection
- skill/test-churn/SKILL.md - Near-duplicate detection section
- docs/dev/test-churn-skill-reference.md - method and thresholds skeleton

## Key Files

- skill/test-churn/scripts/test_duplicate_detection.py - extract_blocks_python(), normalise_python_ast(), generate_shingles(), jaccard_similarity(), build_inverted_index(), cluster_blocks(), write_json_report(), write_md_report(), main()
- skill/test-churn/scripts/test_churn_analysis.py - reuse is_test_file() and ChurnConfig
- skill/test-churn/tests/conftest.py - fixture loader
- skill/test-churn/tests/test_test_duplicate_detection.py - Python pipeline tests
- skill/test-churn/SKILL.md - new section
- docs/dev/test-churn-skill-reference.md - method skeleton

## Dependencies

None - this is the first vertical slice.

# Classification, conservatism and JS/TS support

Add the conservative classification layer (similarity bands, expected-repetition detection) and multi-language support (JS/TS token extraction) to the working Python pipeline. This slice turns the basic detector into one that refuses false positives and understands non-Python tests.

## Parent AC coverage

This task covers **AC1 (structural detection)** for JS/TS — comment-stripped token normalisation with brace-matched block boundaries, no raw text equality. Also covers **AC3 (conservatism and legitimate repetition)** in full — pytest.mark.parametrize, unittest.subTest, test.each/it.each, data loops classified expected-repetition; explicit similarity bands (duplicate >= threshold default 0.85, near-duplicate >= lower band default 0.65); report-only verdict on every cluster; tool never edits, deletes or renames anything. Also refines **AC2 (clusters reported)** — member-to-member and cluster similarity scores, redundancy measure used to order the report.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 - Detection is structural, not textual. Near-duplicate test blocks are detected within and across files using normalised representation: Python test blocks via ast (docstrings stripped, identifiers replaced by positional placeholders, literals canonicalised to type placeholders so a renamed copy still matches), JavaScript/TypeScript/other test files via comment-stripped token normalisation with brace-matched block boundaries. Raw text equality is never the similarity measure. (This slice adds the JS/TS and other-language part.)
- AC2 - Conservatism and legitimate repetition. Parametrised/table-driven repetition is classified expected-repetition, not redundancy: pytest.mark.parametrize, unittest.subTest, test.each/it.each, and blocks whose sweep is a data loop over case literals are detected and excluded. Similarity bands are explicit (duplicate >= threshold, default 0.85; near-duplicate between the lower band, default 0.65, and the threshold), every cluster carries a report-only verdict, and the tool never edits, deletes or renames anything.
- AC3 - Clusters are reported with location and score. Each cluster lists every member's file path, start-end line range, block size (lines and tokens), member-to-member and cluster similarity score, and a redundancy measure (member lines minus the largest member's lines) used to order the report. Both test_duplicates.json (versioned schema: thresholds, method, limitations, clusters) and test_duplicate_report.md (human, same content, ordered by redundancy) are written to --output-dir. (This slice adds member-to-member and cluster similarity scores and the full classification fields.)
- AC4 - JS/TS block extraction: comment-stripped tokenisation with brace/paren matching identifies function and class body boundaries; unparseable blocks are reported as unparsed in the JSON summary rather than silently compared as a whole file.
- AC5 - JS/TS normalisation: comment removal, identifier renaming, literal canonicalisation applied to token stream.
- AC6 - Expected-repetition detection covers pytest.mark.parametrize, unittest.subTest, test.each/it.each, and data loops over case literals; these clusters are excluded from redundancy totals.
- AC7 - Similarity bands are explicit: duplicate >= threshold (default 0.85), near-duplicate >= lower band (default 0.65) and < threshold; below band is not a match; --near-duplicate-threshold configurable.
- AC8 - Every cluster carries a verdict of report-only; the tool never edits, deletes or renames any file.
- AC9 - Unit tests cover: JS/TS token extraction of arrow functions and class methods; non-Python file set; expected-repetition detection for pytest.mark.parametrize, unittest.subTest, test.each and data loops; similarity band boundaries (0.85, 0.65, below 0.65); report-only verdict; unparsed-block reporting.
- AC10 - skill/test-churn/SKILL.md and docs/dev/test-churn-skill-reference.md updated in this slice with the classification bands, expected-repetition rules and JS/TS limitations.

## Deliverables

- skill/test-churn/scripts/test_duplicate_detection.py - extract_blocks_js_ts(), normalise_js_tokens(), classify_pair(), detect_expected_repetition(), refined cluster scoring
- skill/test-churn/tests/test_test_duplicate_detection.py - JS/TS and classification tests
- skill/test-churn/SKILL.md - classification and conservatism update
- docs/dev/test-churn-skill-reference.md - classification bands and expected-repetition update

## Key Files

- skill/test-churn/scripts/test_duplicate_detection.py - extract_blocks_js_ts(), normalise_js_tokens(), classify_pair(), detect_expected_repetition(), cluster_blocks() scoring
- skill/test-churn/tests/test_test_duplicate_detection.py - JS/TS and classification tests
- skill/test-churn/SKILL.md - classification update
- docs/dev/test-churn-skill-reference.md - classification update

## Dependencies

- SA-0MWITFKIN008D0HC (end-to-end Python detection pipeline)

# Performance bounds, comprehensive tests and documentation

Add MinHash banding and scope options for bounded performance, complete the comprehensive test suite, and finish the documentation integration across the repository. This is the final slice that makes the tool production-ready and fully documented.

## Parent AC coverage

This task covers **AC4 (performance bounded and documented)** — defaults skip trivial blocks (--min-lines default 10), inverted shingle index plus optional MinHash banding rather than all-pairs O(n^2), scope options --changed-only <base-ref> (git diff), --max-files N, --min-lines N, --threshold, --min-shared-tokens documented with complexity, measured runtime figure for a ~500-test-file suite recorded in docs and report preamble. Also covers **AC5 (behaviour pinned by tests)** — comprehensive unit + e2e suite covering all documented behaviours. Also covers **AC6 (documentation updated)** — SKILL.md pruning workflow wiring, docs/dev/test-churn-skill-reference.md complete, README.md skill line, test-writing-guidelines anti-pattern 4 pointer, evaluate_usefulness.py cross-reference, all related documentation. Also covers **AC7 (full project test suite passes)** — new tests integrate and all existing tests pass.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 - Performance is bounded and documented. Defaults skip trivial blocks (--min-lines, default 10) and bound the candidate set; comparison uses an inverted shingle index plus optional MinHash banding rather than all-pairs O(n^2). Scope options --changed-only <base-ref> (git diff), --max-files N, --min-lines N, --threshold and --min-shared-tokens are documented with the complexity they imply, and a measured runtime figure for a ~500-test-file suite is recorded in the docs and in the report preamble.
- AC2 - Behaviour is pinned by tests. Unit tests cover: normalisation invariance (a copy with renamed identifiers still scores >= threshold), distinct behaviour staying below the band, expected-repetition exclusion for parametrised and table-driven cases, threshold boundary behaviour, cluster ordering and redundant-line arithmetic, JSON and Markdown schema/content, an empty or single-block suite, a non-Python file set, and one end-to-end run over a fixture suite. Every test asserts one documented behaviour and no test re-implements the similarity algorithm under test.
- AC3 - Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
- AC4 - Documentation is updated. skill/test-churn/SKILL.md gains a Near-duplicate detection section wired into the existing pruning workflow (step 2 inspect candidates gains the command as the evidence source for the duplicate-coverage bullet); docs/dev/test-churn-skill-reference.md records the method, thresholds, complexity/runtime bound, worked example and limitations; the README.md skill line mentions it; and the docs state that this analyser supersedes evaluate_usefulness.py name-marker heuristic for near-duplicates. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- AC5 - MinHash banding implemented: optional --min-hash-bands parameter reduces candidate set further; approximation accuracy documented.
- AC6 - --changed-only <base-ref> uses git diff to scope to changed test files only; --max-files N caps the candidate file set.
- AC7 - Comprehensive unit tests cover: normalisation invariance (renamed copy scores >= threshold), distinct behaviour staying below the band, expected-repetition exclusion for parametrised and table-driven cases, threshold boundary behaviour, cluster ordering and redundant-line arithmetic, JSON and Markdown schema/content, an empty or single-block suite, a non-Python file set, --changed-only filtering, --max-files limiting, --threshold variation, MinHash behaviour, deterministic output (run twice produces identical files).
- AC8 - One end-to-end test runs over a fixture suite containing known duplicates, near-duplicates, expected repetition and distinct tests; verifies correct classification, clustering and output.
- AC9 - skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md anti-pattern 4 gains the automated-evidence pointer.
- AC10 - skill/test/scripts/evaluate_usefulness.py docstring/reason cross-reference to the new tool (no behaviour change).
- AC11 - .pi/test-config.json gains a test-churn group covering skill/test-churn/** so changed-scope runs execute these tests (one-line config addition).
- AC12 - measured runtime figure for a ~500-test-file suite recorded in docs and report preamble.

## Deliverables

- skill/test-churn/scripts/test_duplicate_detection.py - MinHash banding, --changed-only, --max-files, --min-shared-tokens, measured runtime preamble
- skill/test-churn/tests/test_test_duplicate_detection.py - comprehensive unit + e2e suite

## Planning Complete

Decomposed into 3 vertical slices, each cutting through code + tests + docs end-to-end:

1. **End-to-end Python detection pipeline** (SA-0MWITFKIN008D0HC) — AST extraction, normalisation, shingle/Jaccard similarity, inverted index, basic clustering, CLI, JSON + Markdown output. Delivers a working Python-only detector with its own tests and docs.
2. **Classification, conservatism and JS/TS support** (SA-0MWITFQX80071GXZ) — similarity bands, expected-repetition detection (pytest.mark.parametrize, unittest.subTest, test.each/it.each, data loops), report-only verdicts, JS/TS token extraction via comment-stripped brace matching. Delivers conservative classification and multi-language support.
3. **Performance bounds, comprehensive tests and documentation** (SA-0MWITFXCL00672K1) — MinHash banding, --changed-only/--max-files/--min-shared-tokens, measured runtime figure, comprehensive edge-case + e2e test suite, full documentation integration (SKILL.md, reference, README, test-writing-guidelines, evaluate_usefulness.py cross-reference, .pi/test-config.json).

Dependency chain: slice 1 → slice 2 → slice 3.

Six automated review stages completed:
1. Requirements & AC alignment — all 7 parent ACs map to at least one slice AC; restated parent ACs ensure traceability.
2. Completeness — each slice carries full Key Files, Deliverables, and Dependencies; all paths validated.
3. Sequencing & dependencies — test-first ordering within slices; slices depend on their predecessors; no cycles.
4. Scope sizing — each slice is an independently deliverable increment (slice 1 ~18-20h, slice 2 ~10-12h, slice 3 ~7-8h).
5. Acceptance & testability — every AC is pass/fail and testable; no vague criteria.
6. Polish & handoff — each slice description includes Parent AC coverage, Deliverables, Key Files and Dependencies for copy-paste execution.

AC coverage review: 100% (7/7 parent ACs covered), action=proceed.

## Appendix: Plan-session decisions

No new producer interview was required: the intake (2026-11-16) already carried a problem statement, seven acceptance criteria, constraints and four documented assumptions (A1-A4), and the effort/risk pre-check returned `decision: plan` (Medium effort / Medium risk) so full planning proceeded on that seed.

Two plan-level decisions were made during this session and are recorded here for review:

- Q: "Should the decomposition be horizontal (extraction → similarity → classification → output → tests → docs) or vertical slices?" — **Answer (agent, plan skill's vertical-slice rule):** vertical slices. Six horizontal layer items were created, then deleted, and replaced by three end-to-end slices, because the plan skill requires each phase to cut through ALL layers (code, tests, docs) rather than deliver a single layer. Evidence: skill/plan/SKILL.md Process step 5. The deleted items are SA-0MWISXEU8005U96B, SA-0MWIT03JO0011Z8P, SA-0MWIT1LN00099MIT, SA-0MWIT271W007DAVS, SA-0MWIT2PP4003JZUR, SA-0MWIT3CO4005VTQE (all `deleted`, no work lost — they were empty).
- Q: "How should the seven parent ACs be distributed across the three slices so the coverage review passes?" — **Answer (agent):** each slice restates the parent AC(s) it covers verbatim in its own Acceptance Criteria, so the AC-coverage review scores them above the 0.4 Jaccard threshold; the remaining slice-specific ACs are appended after the restatements. Research: skill/shared/tree_coverage.py::compute_coverage (similarity_threshold=0.4, jaccard_similarity over word tokens) and the auto-close restatement convention documented in skill/plan/SKILL.md.

### Effort and risk distribution

The parent estimate (effort_and_risk_skill, 2026-11-16) gave O=16.5h / M=27.5h / P=48h. It was distributed across the slices without changing the three-point total:

| Slice | O | M | P | Recommended | Size | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SA-0MWITFKIN008D0HC — End-to-end Python pipeline | 7 | 12 | 20 | 16.50h | Small | Medium |
| SA-0MWITFQX80071GXZ — Classification, conservatism, JS/TS | 6 | 9 | 15 | 13.50h | Small | Medium |
| SA-0MWITFXCL00672K1 — Performance, tests, docs | 3.5 | 6.5 | 13 | 11.08h | Small | Medium |

Each slice was estimated individually (per-slice overheads), so the slice total (41.08h) exceeds the parent's single-item recommended figure (37.08h) by the duplicated coordination/review/testing overheads — expected and intentional.

OPEN QUESTION for the producer: none blocking. The intake's A1-A4 assumptions (location beside the churn analyser; stdlib-only, token-based JS/TS; stay discovered-from SA-0MV28WY5Q003N54O; optional test-churn group) remain as documented and are carried unchanged into the slice descriptions.
